short: Reaches 2.5% online large-vocabulary WER and 248 h of home use in one participant; rapid calibration is a cross-study claim and the 97.5% conversation accuracy matches the Copy Task figure.
position: The paper [@card2024] changes calibration data (M03), array placement (M05) and sustained home use (M13); each is standard by the verdict rules (one participant, no within-participant ablation). Its final Copy Task sessions reach 2.5% online WER on 125,000 words, the lowest online large-vocabulary WER among the topic's ledger candidates (Appendix), against 23.8% for T12 [@willett2023]; the gap crosses participant, placement, language models and months of accumulated data (2.5% by session 15). Rapid calibration holds only as a description: 9.8% WER after about 473 sentences, within one T12 day (inference), is a lower WER at a similar quantity, not less data. The strongest overreach is the abstract's 97.5% accuracy for conversations, which equals 100 minus the Copy Task 2.5% (inference); measured conversational WER is 3.7% in selected sessions. Home use over 8.4 months is the real advance; other users remain untested, as the authors concede.
